title: 走一步看一步 EP01｜台北女巫店和她的三十年
title_en: Taipei's Witch House: Thirty Years of Indie Music and Women's Spaces
summary_cn: 从台大旁一栋「楼上女书店」的一楼店面，到台湾独立音乐的孕育之地，女巫店从来不是精心规划的产物：创始人彭郁晶是学烹饪的餐饮学徒，半推半就开店；一车从倒闭 Livehouse 拉来的器材，让这里意外有了演出；被邻居噪音投诉逼出的「不插电」，反而成就了她。三十年过去，她像一棵老榕树——不是最新最炫的，但一直在那里
summary_en: From a shoebox storefront beneath a women's bookstore beside NTU to the birthplace of Taiwan's indie music, the Witch House was never a carefully planned project: founder Peng Yujing was a pastry apprentice who opened the shop half-willingly; a truckload of gear rescued from a shut-down livehouse accidentally turned it into a stage; and noise complaints forced the 'unplugged' rule that made its name. Thirty years on, it's like an old banyan tree — not the flashiest thing around, but always there.

scenes.title_cn: 一、稀里糊涂的开始：从餐饮梦到女巫店 [00:00–05:16]
scenes.title_en: A Chaotic Beginning: From a Cooking Dream to the Witch House
scenes.context: The hosts set the scene: Taiwan lifted martial law in 1987, and by the early nineties society was restless for an outlet of expression — underground bands and rock livehouses were popping up. Then they introduce founder Peng Yujing, a sociology grad who couldn't find work and dreamed of running her own restaurant. 语域：casual storytelling + 历史背景讲解。
scenes.speak: In 1987, Taiwan officially lifted martial law, ending 38 years of military rule. Like someone who hasn't been allowed to speak for ages finally getting room to breathe, society in the early nineties was itching to move — everyone was looking for an outlet for expression. Underground bands appeared, and livehouses built for rock fans, like Xilang, Rengou, and Mayi, slowly came into being. The key insight: a society's outlet for expression comes before business logic. Livehouses aren't just performance venues — they're physical spaces for 'speaking out.' The soil for indie music is basically the bottled-up urge to express released after martial law. Typical scenario: to understand why Taiwan's indie music burst out all at once in the nineties — you need a society that can talk before you get musicians who dare to express themselves. Quote from the show: 'Martial law had just ended after those decades, the whole society was restless, everyone was looking for an outlet for expression.' How this connects to the Witch House: it's one of the space-products of this wave of expression — but what makes it special is the three principles that reality later forced out of it. Meet the founder: Peng Yujing studied sociology at National Taiwan University, but couldn't find a job after graduating. She loved food, so she completed a cooking program, apprenticed in the pastry kitchen of the Sherwood Hotel, and dreamed of one day opening a restaurant of her own.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：1987 年台湾正式解除戒严令，结束长达 38 年的军事管制。像一个人憋了很久没说话、终于得到可以喘气的机会，九十年代初整个社会蠢蠢欲动，都在寻找表达的出口——地下乐团出现，西朗、人狗、蚂蚁等为摇滚乐迷打造的 Livehouse 也慢慢出现
sentences.en: In 1987, Taiwan officially lifted martial law, ending 38 years of military rule. Like someone who hasn't been allowed to speak for ages finally getting room to breathe, society in the early nineties was itching to move — everyone was looking for an outlet for expression. Underground bands appeared, and livehouses built for rock fans, like Xilang, Rengou, and Mayi, slowly came into being.
sentences.note: 表达提示martial law → 戒严令；lift / end martial law → 解除戒严；an outlet for expression → 表达的出口；underground band → 地下乐团；room to breathe → 喘息空间

sentences.cn: 关键理解：一个社会的表达出口先于商业逻辑出现。Livehouse 不只是演出场地，更是「说话」的物理空间；独立音乐的土壤，本质是解严后释放的表达欲
sentences.en: The key insight: a society's outlet for expression comes before business logic. Livehouses aren't just performance venues — they're physical spaces for 'speaking out.' The soil for indie music is basically the bottled-up urge to express released after martial law.
sentences.note: 表达提示come before → 先于…出现；business logic → 商业逻辑；speak out → 发声；bottled-up → 憋着/压抑已久的；the soil for … → 孕育…的土壤

sentences.cn: 典型场景：理解台湾独立音乐为什么在 90 年代集中爆发——先有「能说话」的社会，才有敢表达的音乐人
sentences.en: Typical scenario: to understand why Taiwan's indie music burst out all at once in the nineties — you need a society that can talk before you get musicians who dare to express themselves.
sentences.note: 表达提示burst out / explode → 集中爆发；dare to … → 敢于…；music scene → 音乐圈/音乐生态

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据：「那几十年的戒严刚结束，整个社会也蠢蠢欲动，大家都在寻找一个表达的出口。」
sentences.en: Quote from the show: 'Martial law had just ended after those decades, the whole society was restless, everyone was looking for an outlet for expression.'
sentences.note: 表达提示restless → 蠢蠢欲动/坐不住；Quote from the show → 节目原话；restless vs anxious：前者是躁动地想行动，后者是焦虑

sentences.cn: （引用）与女巫店的关系：女巫店正是这一波表达潮流的空间产物之一，但它的特殊性来自后面被逼出来的三原则
sentences.en: How this connects to the Witch House: it's one of the space-products of this wave of expression — but what makes it special is the three principles that reality later forced out of it.
sentences.note: 表达提示a product of its time → 时代的产物；wave of expression → 表达潮流；force sth out of sb → 从某人身上逼出…

sentences.cn: 核心机制：彭郁晶就读台大社会学系，毕业后找不到工作。她喜欢美食，便去烹饪学校完成烹飪课程，又到西华饭店点心房当学徒，梦想是开一间属于自己的餐饮店
sentences.en: Meet the founder: Peng Yujing studied sociology at National Taiwan University, but couldn't find a job after graduating. She loved food, so she completed a cooking program, apprenticed in the pastry kitchen of the Sherwood Hotel, and dreamed of one day opening a restaurant of her own.
sentences.note: 表达提示sociology → 社会学；apprentice → 学徒；pastry kitchen → 点心房；of one's own → 属于自己的；dream of doing → 梦想做…

paraphrase.intent: 想说「整个社会都在找表达的出口」
phrases: The whole society was hungry for a way to speak up.
Everyone was looking for somewhere — anywhere — to let their voice out.
paraphrase.chunks: hungry for · a way to speak up · let their voice out
paraphrase.usage: hungry for 比 looking for 更有渴望感；speak up 侧重公开发声

paraphrase.intent: 想说「先有能说话的社会，才有敢表达的音乐人」
phrases: You can't have daring musicians without a society that lets them talk.
The music scene was just the voice of a society finally allowed to speak.
paraphrase.chunks: you can't have A without B · a society finally allowed to speak
paraphrase.usage: You can't have A without B 是强调因果的常用句型

scenes.title_cn: 二、阿峰与 Scum：摇滚噪音付出的代价
scenes.title_en: A-Feng and Scum: The Price of Rock & Roll Noise
scenes.context: A-Feng of the indie band Boney Flesh opened Scum, a performance space near NTU with a rare rule: bands had to play original songs. Loud rock noise brought neighbor complaints, police fines, and finally the venue's death — but the borrowed gear became the Witch House's first stage. 语域：narrative storytelling + 人物故事。
scenes.speak: A-Feng, a member of the indie band Boney Flesh — not the A-Feng from Sodagreen — founded Scum, a performance space near NTU. Unlike other livehouses that allowed full cover sets, Scum was one of the first venues to require bands on stage to play original songs. The key insight: that 'originals only' rule planted the seed of Taiwan's indie scene. But back then underground bands mostly played rock, and the ear-splitting volume drew neighbor complaints and police fines. A-Feng sank his own money in, lost a Mercedes in the process, and the venue finally went under. Typical scenario: when a 'righteous principle' collides with physical reality — noise complaints, in this case — an idea with no room for compromise gets crushed by cost. This is the cautionary tale the Witch House later took most seriously. Quote from the show: 'Scum was one of the very first places to require bands to play an original song on stage.' How this connects: Scum's original-song spirit was inherited by the Witch House, while its noise lesson was avoided by the Witch House's 'unplugged' approach. After Scum closed, A-Feng asked Peng Yujing whether he could borrow the music gear from his old venue so they could perform in her new space. It was a full truckload. Peng didn't think twice — a public space can be used in many ways, not just for food — so she agreed, and even let them handle the sound.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：独立乐团骨皮肉成员阿峰（不是苏打绿的阿峰）在台大附近创立展演空间 Scum。与其他允许全翻唱的 Livehouse 不同，Scum 几乎是最早一批规定「上台乐团必须演奏原创曲目」的地方
sentences.en: A-Feng, a member of the indie band Boney Flesh — not the A-Feng from Sodagreen — founded Scum, a performance space near NTU. Unlike other livehouses that allowed full cover sets, Scum was one of the first venues to require bands on stage to play original songs.
sentences.note: 表达提示cover set / cover song → 翻唱曲目；original song → 原创曲目；performance space / venue → 展演空间；band member → 乐团成员

sentences.cn: 关键理解：「必须原创」埋下了台湾独立乐团发展的种子。但当时地下乐团多演摇滚，超高声贝的噪音引来居民投诉抗议，Scum 吃了大量警察罚单——阿峰把赚的倒贴进去，还赔掉一台奔驰，最终倒闭
sentences.en: The key insight: that 'originals only' rule planted the seed of Taiwan's indie scene. But back then underground bands mostly played rock, and the ear-splitting volume drew neighbor complaints and police fines. A-Feng sank his own money in, lost a Mercedes in the process, and the venue finally went under.
sentences.note: 表达提示plant the seed of → 埋下…的种子；ear-splitting → 震耳欲聋的；police fine → 警察罚单；go under → 倒闭；sink money in → 把钱倒贴进去

sentences.cn: 典型场景：当「理念正确」撞上「物理现实」（噪音扰民），没有妥协机制的理念会被成本压垮——这是女巫店后来最重要的反面教材
sentences.en: Typical scenario: when a 'righteous principle' collides with physical reality — noise complaints, in this case — an idea with no room for compromise gets crushed by cost. This is the cautionary tale the Witch House later took most seriously.
sentences.note: 表达提示collide with reality → 与现实相撞；cautionary tale → 反面教材；no room for compromise → 没有妥协空间；get crushed by cost → 被成本压垮

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据：「Scum 几乎是最早一批规定，上台的乐团必须演奏一首原创曲目的地方。」
sentences.en: Quote from the show: 'Scum was one of the very first places to require bands to play an original song on stage.'
sentences.note: 表达提示one of the very first → 最早一批之一（very 表强调）；on stage → 上台演出

sentences.cn: （引用）与女巫店的关系：Scum 的原创理念被女巫店继承，噪音的教训被女巫店的「不插电」规避
sentences.en: How this connects: Scum's original-song spirit was inherited by the Witch House, while its noise lesson was avoided by the Witch House's 'unplugged' approach.
sentences.note: 表达提示inherit → 继承；avoid / dodge → 规避；unplugged → 不插电

sentences.cn: 核心机制：关了店的阿峰找到彭郁晶，问她能否借出之前 Scum 店里的音乐器材，让他们在新空间表演。器材足足有一车，彭郁晶没想太多——她认为公共空间的运用有很多种，不一定只做餐饮——便同意阿峰他们来表演，也顺便让他们安排音控
sentences.en: After Scum closed, A-Feng asked Peng Yujing whether he could borrow the music gear from his old venue so they could perform in her new space. It was a full truckload. Peng didn't think twice — a public space can be used in many ways, not just for food — so she agreed, and even let them handle the sound.
sentences.note: 表达提示gear / equipment → 器材；a truckload of → 一车的；not think twice → 没多想；handle the sound → 安排音控

paraphrase.intent: 想说「理念撞上现实后被成本压垮」
phrases: The principle got crushed by the running costs.
A great idea doesn't survive contact with noise complaints and fines.
paraphrase.chunks: get crushed by · doesn't survive contact with
paraphrase.usage: crushed by cost 直接有力；survive contact with 是带点幽默的说法

paraphrase.intent: 想说「他把钱全倒贴进去了」
phrases: He sank every penny of his earnings into it.
All the money he made went straight back into the venue.
paraphrase.chunks: sink money into · go straight back into
paraphrase.usage: sink money into 偏书面；went straight back into 更口语、有画面感

scenes.title_cn: 三、女巫店三原则：被现状逼出来的定调 [08:26]
scenes.title_en: The Witch House's Three Rules: Principles Forced by Reality
scenes.context: The Witch House sits in a residential area near NTU, on the ground floor of a space too small to soundproof — it couldn't copy Scum's full underground-band model. So Peng made three decisions: unplugged, originals only, and female-first. The constraints weren't flaws; they were reframed as advantages. 语域：商业/定位分析 + 讲故事。
scenes.speak: The Witch House sits in a residential area near NTU, on the ground floor, in a space so small that installing soundproofing was nearly impossible. Even with Scum's original crew running it, the full underground-band model couldn't be copied into this brand-new little room — or they'd get fined and shut down just the same. At the same time, more macho rock livehouses like Vibes were popping up. So Peng searched for the style that fit the Witch House best and made a three-point decision. The key insight: the three principles interlock into one system — unplugged solves 'whether we can survive', original music solves 'what we become', and female-first solves 'who gets to define us.' The constraints weren't treated as flaws; they were reframed into an advantage to be exploited. Quote from the show: 'Later she made a decision, including three points... none of these have to be limits — they can actually become an advantage you can use.' Unplugged was less a musical stance than a compromise forced by worrying the neighbors would complain. But at the same time it was an encouragement — an invitation to look beyond rock's loudness and find the craft of getting the audience more involved when you're performing up close. The key insight: compromise isn't retreating — it's competing on a different track. The noise restriction moved the competition from 'volume' to 'intimacy and skill', and that became the Witch House's differentiation advantage. Typical scenario: when resources, space, and compliance are all constrained, translating 'what we can't do' into 'what we can do better' is the most cost-effective way to position yourself.

sentences.cn: 女巫店位于台大附近的居民区、店面在一楼且空间小、很难装隔音设备；即使让 Scum 原班人马操持，也没法把地下乐团整套模式复制进这个新开不久的小空间，否则照样吃罚单关门。同期又出现 Vibes 等阳刚摇滚风格的 Livehouse。彭郁晶由此探索最适合女巫店的风格，做了一个三点决定：
sentences.en: The Witch House sits in a residential area near NTU, on the ground floor, in a space so small that installing soundproofing was nearly impossible. Even with Scum's original crew running it, the full underground-band model couldn't be copied into this brand-new little room — or they'd get fined and shut down just the same. At the same time, more macho rock livehouses like Vibes were popping up. So Peng searched for the style that fit the Witch House best and made a three-point decision.
sentences.note: 表达提示residential area → 居民区；soundproofing → 隔音设备；copy / transplant a model → 复制模式；macho → 阳刚的；get fined and shut down → 吃罚单关门

sentences.cn: 关键理解：三条原则互相咬合成一个系统：不插电解决「能不能活」，原创解决「活成什么样」，女性优先解决「谁来定义」。限制没有被当成缺陷，而是被转念成可利用的优势
sentences.en: The key insight: the three principles interlock into one system — unplugged solves 'whether we can survive', original music solves 'what we become', and female-first solves 'who gets to define us.' The constraints weren't treated as flaws; they were reframed into an advantage to be exploited.
sentences.note: 表达提示interlock → 互相咬合；reframe → 重新框定/转念；an advantage to be exploited → 可利用的优势；constraint vs flaw → 限制 vs 缺陷

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据：「后来她做了一个决定，包括三点……这些其实都不必成为限制，反而可以成为一种可利用的优势。」
sentences.en: Quote from the show: 'Later she made a decision, including three points... none of these have to be limits — they can actually become an advantage you can use.'
sentences.note: 表达提示None of these have to be limits → 这些都不必成为限制；turn into an advantage → 转化为优势

sentences.cn: 核心机制：与其说 Unplugged 是一种音乐立场，不如说是担心邻居嫌吵、被现状逼出来的妥协。但它同时是鼓励——鼓励表演者在摇滚的喧嚣之外，去寻找「你和观众近距离时，怎么让他更投入」的技巧与法门
sentences.en: Unplugged was less a musical stance than a compromise forced by worrying the neighbors would complain. But at the same time it was an encouragement — an invitation to look beyond rock's loudness and find the craft of getting the audience more involved when you're performing up close.
sentences.note: 表达提示less A than B → 与其说是A不如说是B；stance / position → 立场；get sb involved → 让某人更投入；up close → 近距离

sentences.cn: 关键理解：妥协不是退让，而是换一条路竞争。噪音限制把竞争维度从「音量」切换到了「亲密感与技巧」——这反而成为女巫店的差异化优势
sentences.en: The key insight: compromise isn't retreating — it's competing on a different track. The noise restriction moved the competition from 'volume' to 'intimacy and skill', and that became the Witch House's differentiation advantage.
sentences.note: 表达提示retreat → 退让；compete on a different track → 换一条赛道竞争；differentiation → 差异化；edge / differentiator → 优势

sentences.cn: 典型场景：在资源、场地、合规都受限时，把「不能做的事」翻译成「可以做得更好的事」，是最高性价比的定位方法
sentences.en: Typical scenario: when resources, space, and compliance are all constrained, translating 'what we can't do' into 'what we can do better' is the most cost-effective way to position yourself.
sentences.note: 表达提示cost-effective → 性价比高的；position yourself → 定位自己；compliance → 合规；translate A into B → 把A转化成B

paraphrase.intent: 想说「与其说是立场，不如说是被逼的妥协」
phrases: Unplugged was less a statement than a forced compromise.
It wasn't a musical stance so much as a rule the neighbors handed her.
paraphrase.chunks: less A than B · not so much A as B
paraphrase.usage: less A than B / not so much A as B 是同一意思的两种常用结构

phrases: She turned every constraint into a competitive edge.
The very thing that limited her became her selling point.
paraphrase.chunks: turn A into B · the very thing that … became …
paraphrase.usage: the very thing 表强调，口语里很出彩

scenes.title_cn: 四、女性空间：从观众席走上舞台 [13:08]
scenes.title_en: A Women's Space: From the Audience to the Stage
scenes.context: The Witch House's website keeps a 'Time Tunnel' timeline of first performances since 1996 — Chen Shan-Ni, Huang Xiaozhen, Chen Qizhen, and Anpu all debuted there. One day a month, 'Witch Festival' features only female performers. The store's menu and decor openly embrace women's bodies and pleasure. 语域：文化观察 + 女性主义话题。
scenes.speak: The Witch House's website keeps a timeline called the 'Time Tunnel' recording the first performances of many bands and artists since 1996. In the opening year, 1996, the stage still belonged to rock bands like Quarterback and Boney Flesh; Chen Shan-Ni only showed up at year's end. From 1997, Huang Xiaozhen, Yi Nengjing, and Chen Qizhen followed one after another, then Panai in 1998, and Lei Guangxia plus a not-yet-debuted Anpu in 1999. Also, one day each month is 'Witch Festival', when only female singers can perform. The key insight: the Witch Festival gave female creators their first stage of their own, and definitively set the Witch House apart from every other music space — on one side machismo and soundwaves, on the other stars and artistry. Typical scenario: to support an overlooked group, don't offer an 'equal invitation' — build a tilted stage instead, with a fixed time and a fixed mechanism for making room. Quote from the show: 'Female creators had their own stage for the first time, and this completely separated the Witch House's picture from other music spaces — one side is machismo and soundwaves, the other is stars and artistry.' From the start, Peng positioned the Witch House as 'a place where girls can stay out late.' The food proudly calls itself 'the most mischievous menu challenging the limits of human taste': Menstruation Iced Tea, Wine-Pool Meat-Shower, and Wild Strawberries. There's also an unwritten rule — if you dare to take off your bra and hang it on your chair, your drink is free. Peng jokes that, for hygiene reasons, they do hope everyone rotates their bras regularly. The walls are covered with posters of female rock musicians and dolls of every kind, the bathroom walls carry essays on female orgasm, and sanitary products are stocked for women. The key insight: putting 'things we're taught to feel embarrassed about' into public space is itself a feminist spatial practice — it sends the message that these things are nothing to be ashamed of.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：女巫店官网有名为「时光隧道」的年表，记录 1996 年以来许多乐团乐手的首次演出时间：开业第一年（1996）还是四分卫、骨皮这类摇滚乐队，年底才出现陈珊妮；从 1997 年开始，黄小桢、伊能静、陈绮贞陆续出现，1998 年巴奈，1999 年雷光夏和当时还未出道的安溥。此外，每个月有一天「女巫祭」，当天只有女性歌手可以演出
sentences.en: The Witch House's website keeps a timeline called the 'Time Tunnel' recording the first performances of many bands and artists since 1996. In the opening year, 1996, the stage still belonged to rock bands like Quarterback and Boney Flesh; Chen Shan-Ni only showed up at year's end. From 1997, Huang Xiaozhen, Yi Nengjing, and Chen Qizhen followed one after another, then Panai in 1998, and Lei Guangxia plus a not-yet-debuted Anpu in 1999. Also, one day each month is 'Witch Festival', when only female singers can perform.
sentences.note: 表达提示timeline → 时间线/年表；debut → 首次演出/出道；one after another → 陆续；show up → 出现

sentences.cn: 关键理解：「女巫祭」让女性创作者第一次有了属于自己的舞台，也让女巫店的调性彻底与其他音乐空间分开：一边是阳刚和音浪，一边是星星与文艺
sentences.en: The key insight: the Witch Festival gave female creators their first stage of their own, and definitively set the Witch House apart from every other music space — on one side machismo and soundwaves, on the other stars and artistry.
sentences.note: 表达提示set apart from → 与…区分开；machismo → 阳刚气/大男子气；artistry → 文艺气息；a stage of one's own → 属于自己的舞台

sentences.cn: 典型场景：当你想支持一个被忽视的群体，与其做「平等的邀请」，不如做「倾斜的舞台」——固定时间、固定机制地让位
sentences.en: Typical scenario: to support an overlooked group, don't offer an 'equal invitation' — build a tilted stage instead, with a fixed time and a fixed mechanism for making room.
sentences.note: 表达提示overlooked group → 被忽视的群体；tilted stage → 倾斜的舞台（结构性让位）；make room for → 为…腾出位置

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据：「女性创作者们第一次有了属于自己的舞台，这也让女巫店的图景彻底和其他的音乐空间去分开。一边是阳刚和音浪的，另外一边是星星、文艺的。」
sentences.en: Quote from the show: 'Female creators had their own stage for the first time, and this completely separated the Witch House's picture from other music spaces — one side is machismo and soundwaves, the other is stars and artistry.'
sentences.note: 表达提示Separate A from B → 把A和B分开；the picture / the vibe → 图景/调性

sentences.cn: 核心机制：彭郁晶一开始就把女巫店定位成「一间女生可以玩很晚的店」。店内餐饮自称「挑战人类极限最调皮的菜单」：月经冰茶、酒池肉淋、纵草莓；还有个不成文规定——只要敢脱下内衣挂在椅子上，就免费获得一杯饮料（彭开玩笑说基于卫生考量，希望大家规律更换内衣）。店里挂着女性摇滚乐手海报、各色女性玩偶，厕所里贴着探索女性性高潮的文章，也为女生准备卫生用品
sentences.en: From the start, Peng positioned the Witch House as 'a place where girls can stay out late.' The food proudly calls itself 'the most mischievous menu challenging the limits of human taste': Menstruation Iced Tea, Wine-Pool Meat-Shower, and Wild Strawberries. There's also an unwritten rule — if you dare to take off your bra and hang it on your chair, your drink is free. Peng jokes that, for hygiene reasons, they do hope everyone rotates their bras regularly. The walls are covered with posters of female rock musicians and dolls of every kind, the bathroom walls carry essays on female orgasm, and sanitary products are stocked for women.
sentences.note: 表达提示unwritten rule → 不成文的规定；mischievous → 调皮的；on the house → 店家免费请客；sanitary products → 卫生用品；stay out late → 在外面玩到很晚

sentences.cn: 关键理解：让「被认为是难为情的东西」出现在公共空间，本身就是一种女性主义的空间实践——它传递的是：这些东西并不值得难为情
sentences.en: The key insight: putting 'things we're taught to feel embarrassed about' into public space is itself a feminist spatial practice — it sends the message that these things are nothing to be ashamed of.
sentences.note: 表达提示feminist spatial practice → 女性主义的空间实践；nothing to be ashamed of → 不值得难为情；send the message → 传递出…信号

paraphrase.intent: 想说「给被忽视的群体让出舞台」
phrases: Don't just invite them equally — hand over the stage.
Give the overlooked group a stage with a guaranteed slot.
paraphrase.chunks: hand over the stage · a guaranteed slot
paraphrase.usage: hand over 有主动让位的力度；guaranteed slot 强调制度性保证

paraphrase.intent: 想说「把难为情的东西摆进公共空间」
phrases: She put the 'unmentionable' right out in the open.
Things nobody dared to talk about got a home on the wall.
paraphrase.chunks: right out in the open · get a home on the wall
paraphrase.usage: out in the open 口语常用；unmentionable 比 embarrassing 更书面些

scenes.title_cn: 五、独立精神不止于音乐 [16:32]
scenes.context: Poetry readings, glove puppetry, and stage plays — the Witch House's independent spirit welcomed any non-commercial expression, not just music. For its 20th anniversary it sold festival tickets by hand, one envelope at a time, cutting out ticketing middlemen. 语域：文化叙事 + 独立精神讨论。
scenes.speak: The independent spirit the Witch House championed was never limited to indie music — it welcomed all kinds of creation and expression that stood apart from commerce. In 1999, Peng's German husband Yo-Yo hosted poetry readings, where Hong Hong and Xia Yu — under her pen name Li Gedi — both read their work, and some people recited with an almost rock-like explosive force, blurring the line between poetry and music. The store also staged A-Chung's glove puppet theater — glove puppetry, which originated in Fujian and grew to full development in Taiwan, is operated by hand and fingers with no human performer, relying on the backstage band; the Witch House was exactly the right venue. Stage plays and other forms followed. The key insight: 'independence' is a creative stance, and music is only one of its faces. A space that refuses to box itself in can keep holding different forms of expression. Typical scenario: keep an entry point in your space or brand for the unplanned — real distinctiveness often comes from the accidents you're willing to catch. Anpu's line: 'A small audience, the performers, and the shop together created a performance atmosphere that didn't need much defining.' Quote from the show: 'She really didn't box herself in tightly. The independent spirit she championed didn't only mean independent music... music is just one of its faces, one of its ways of expression.' For the Witch House's 20th anniversary, they held the 'Witch Festival' music festival, selling tickets completely on their own with no middleman ticketing platform — in today's terms, 'no middleman markup.' They mailed tickets to fans one by one by hand — a very handmade way of doing things.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：女巫店倡导的独立精神不限于独立音乐，也欢迎各种独立于商业的创作与表达。1999 年，彭郁晶的德国丈夫悠悠主持诗歌发表活动，鸿鸿、夏宇（另一个名字李格蒂）都曾发表诗歌，还有人用接近摇滚的爆发力朗诵诗歌，模糊了诗歌与乐曲的界限。店里也上演过阿中偶戏布袋戏——布袋戏起源于福建、在台湾全面发展，靠手指和手掌操控木偶，无真人参与，依赖后场音乐配合，女巫店正是合适的场地；此外还有舞台剧等
sentences.en: The independent spirit the Witch House championed was never limited to indie music — it welcomed all kinds of creation and expression that stood apart from commerce. In 1999, Peng's German husband Yo-Yo hosted poetry readings, where Hong Hong and Xia Yu — under her pen name Li Gedi — both read their work, and some people recited with an almost rock-like explosive force, blurring the line between poetry and music. The store also staged A-Chung's glove puppet theater — glove puppetry, which originated in Fujian and grew to full development in Taiwan, is operated by hand and fingers with no human performer, relying on the backstage band; the Witch House was exactly the right venue. Stage plays and other forms followed.
sentences.note: 表达提示champion → 倡导/力挺；stand apart from → 独立于…；glove puppetry / glove puppet → 布袋戏；blur the line between A and B → 模糊A与B的界限；recite poetry → 朗诵诗歌

sentences.cn: 关键理解：「独立」是一种创作姿态，音乐只是其中一个面向。空间不框死自己，才能持续容纳不同形态的表达
sentences.en: The key insight: 'independence' is a creative stance, and music is only one of its faces. A space that refuses to box itself in can keep holding different forms of expression.
sentences.note: 表达提示creative stance → 创作姿态；one face of it → 其中的一个面向；box oneself in → 把自己框死；hold / host forms of expression → 容纳不同的表达形式

sentences.cn: 典型场景：给你的空间/品牌保留「计划之外」的入口——真正的独特性常来自你愿意接住的意外
sentences.en: Typical scenario: keep an entry point in your space or brand for the unplanned — real distinctiveness often comes from the accidents you're willing to catch.
sentences.note: 表达提示entry point → 入口；distinctiveness → 独特性；catch the accident → 接住意外；leave room for → 为…留出空间

sentences.cn: （引用）「少数的观众、表演者和店家一起营造了一个不太需要定义的表演氛围。」——安溥
sentences.en: Anpu's line: 'A small audience, the performers, and the shop together created a performance atmosphere that didn't need much defining.'
sentences.note: 表达提示atmosphere → 氛围；didn't need much defining → 不太需要被定义；A's line → 某人说过的话

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据：「她真的没有把自己框得很死，她所倡导的独立精神，指的不仅仅是独立音乐……音乐只是其中的一个面向、其中一种表达方式而已。」
sentences.en: Quote from the show: 'She really didn't box herself in tightly. The independent spirit she championed didn't only mean independent music... music is just one of its faces, one of its ways of expression.'
sentences.note: 表达提示box oneself in → 框死自己；mean more than just … → 不仅仅指…；one way of expression → 一种表达方式

sentences.cn: 核心机制：女巫店 20 周年时举办了「女巫祭」音乐节，完全独立售卖、不依赖中间售票商——用今天的话说就是「不要中间商赚差价」——他们用人工一张一张把门票寄给观众，是非常手工的方式
sentences.en: For the Witch House's 20th anniversary, they held the 'Witch Festival' music festival, selling tickets completely on their own with no middleman ticketing platform — in today's terms, 'no middleman markup.' They mailed tickets to fans one by one by hand — a very handmade way of doing things.
sentences.note: 表达提示middleman → 中间商/售票商；no middleman markup → 不要中间商赚差价；by hand / manually → 人工地；handmade / handcrafted → 手工的

paraphrase.intent: 想说「独立是一种姿态，音乐只是其中一面」
phrases: Independence is a stance; music just happens to be the best-known face of it.
Being independent isn't about the genre — it's about the attitude.
paraphrase.chunks: a stance · just one face of it · it's about the attitude
paraphrase.usage: It's about the attitude 是高度口语化的总结句

paraphrase.intent: 想说「不依赖中间商，纯手工卖票」
phrases: They cut out the middleman and mailed every ticket by hand.
No ticketing platform — just envelopes, stamps, and patience.
paraphrase.chunks: cut out the middleman · by hand
paraphrase.usage: cut out 表示剔除，比 remove 口语；envelopes, stamps, and patience 是画面感很强的列举

scenes.title_en: The Slash Space of the Livehouse World
scenes.context: The Witch House has always been a multi-hyphen space: cafe, livehouse, bar, and later board-game tables. After the Taichung ALABAR fire killed nine people, regulations tightened and the Witch House was told its zoning didn't match its business — until supporters rallied and the rules were rewritten. 语域：商业韧性分析 + 政策事件叙事。
scenes.speak: The Witch House has always called itself 'the slash space of the livehouse world': it began as a cafe, then became a livehouse plus a bar. Thursday, Friday, and Saturday at nine in the evening there's always a show, with a 350-TWD cover charge that includes one drink. Later, board games were added — it doesn't rake in big money, but it doesn't die either. The key insight: from today's perspective, doing an indie stage, a cafe, a bar, and board games all at once isn't impressive — it almost sounds ordinary. But precisely because of that messy positioning, not leaning too heavily on music revenue but walking on several legs, the Witch House has managed to run to this day — and it left young creators room to breathe. Typical scenario: 'people really should live a bit messier, and a shop can try to be messier too' — multiple income streams aren't a distraction; they're redundancy by design. Quote from the show: 'Maybe it was precisely because of that messy positioning back then — not leaning too much on income from music shows but walking on many legs — that the Witch House could keep operating smoothly to this day.' Then came the crisis: a fire at the Taichung bar ALABAR claimed nine lives, and regulators finally started taking the livehouse world's long-neglected legal problems seriously. The Witch House got checked again and again, told that its 'zoning use and registered business items didn't meet the standards' — because running a livehouse wasn't exactly legal back then. Under the pressure, Peng thought: 'If the law says no, then fine — I just won't do it anymore.' The turning point was the supporters: after the news spread, fans voiced support online, dropped written opinions into the market's letterbox, and cleared the shelves of the store's merch — far beyond what Peng could have imagined. The authorities then amended the regulations to add a category for 'music performance spaces', legitimizing the livehouse business. That's how the Witch House survived the storm.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：女巫店对自己的定位一直是「Livehouse 界的斜杠空间」：一开始是咖啡馆，然后是 Livehouse 加酒吧；周四、周五、周六晚上九点都有表演，观众入场费 350 台币（约 75 元人民币）且附送一杯饮料。后来又有了桌游——装不了大钱，但也死不了
sentences.en: The Witch House has always called itself 'the slash space of the livehouse world': it began as a cafe, then became a livehouse plus a bar. Thursday, Friday, and Saturday at nine in the evening there's always a show, with a 350-TWD cover charge that includes one drink. Later, board games were added — it doesn't rake in big money, but it doesn't die either.
sentences.note: 表达提示slash / multi-hyphen → 斜杠；cover charge / entry fee → 入场费；rake in money → 赚大钱；board game → 桌游

sentences.cn: 关键理解：从今天的视角看，独立音乐舞台、咖啡馆、酒吧、桌游全都做并不稀奇，甚至有点普通。但也许正是因为当年这样「杂」的定位，没有过度依赖音乐演出的收入，女巫店才能顺利营业至今，也给刚起步的创作者留下能喘气的创作空间
sentences.en: The key insight: from today's perspective, doing an indie stage, a cafe, a bar, and board games all at once isn't impressive — it almost sounds ordinary. But precisely because of that messy positioning, not leaning too heavily on music revenue but walking on several legs, the Witch House has managed to run to this day — and it left young creators room to breathe.
sentences.note: 表达提示messy positioning → 杂的定位；lean too heavily on → 过度依赖；walk on several legs → 多只脚走路；room to breathe → 喘息的空间

sentences.cn: 典型场景：「人果然还是要活得杂一点，店也可以尽力地杂一点」——多元收入不是不务正业，而是组织层面的冗余设计
sentences.en: Typical scenario: 'people really should live a bit messier, and a shop can try to be messier too' — multiple income streams aren't a distraction; they're redundancy by design.
sentences.note: 表达提示income stream → 收入来源；redundancy by design → 组织层面的冗余设计；not a distraction → 不是不务正业

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据：「也许正是因为当年这样杂的一个定位，没有过度依靠音乐演出带来的收入，而是依赖多只脚走路，女巫店才可以顺利的营业至今。」
sentences.en: Quote from the show: 'Maybe it was precisely because of that messy positioning back then — not leaning too much on income from music shows but walking on many legs — that the Witch House could keep operating smoothly to this day.'
sentences.note: 表达提示precisely because → 恰恰因为；operate smoothly → 顺利营业；keep doing to this day → 一直至今

sentences.cn: 核心机制：台中阿拉酒吧一场大火带走 9 条生命，让相关部门开始重视 Livehouse 存在已久的法规问题。女巫店被频繁查访，被告知「分区使用和营业项目不符合标准」——因为在当时做 Livehouse 并不是那么合法的。压力之下彭郁晶想：「既然法律不允许，干，老娘不做总可以了吧。」
sentences.en: A fire at the Taichung bar ALABAR claimed nine lives, and regulators finally started taking the livehouse world's long-neglected legal problems seriously. The Witch House got checked again and again, told that its 'zoning use and registered business items didn't meet the standards' — because running a livehouse wasn't exactly legal back then. Under the pressure, Peng thought: 'If the law says no, then fine — I just won't do it anymore.'
sentences.note: 表达提示claim lives → 夺走生命；zoning use → 分区使用；registered business items → 营业项目；take A seriously → 重视A；regulators / authorities → 相关部门

sentences.cn: 关键理解：转折点是支持者：消息传出后，支持者线上声援、跑到市场信箱表达意见、到店里爆买商品，突破了彭郁晶的想象。相关部门随后修改条例，增加「音乐展演空间业」项目，让 Livehouse 业态得以成立，女巫店才挺过这场风波
sentences.en: The turning point was the supporters: after the news spread, fans voiced support online, dropped written opinions into the market's letterbox, and cleared the shelves of the store's merch — far beyond what Peng could have imagined. The authorities then amended the regulations to add a category for 'music performance spaces', legitimizing the livehouse business. That's how the Witch House survived the storm.
sentences.note: 表达提示turning point → 转折点；voice support → 声援；amend the regulations → 修改条例；legitimize → 使合法化；get through the storm → 挺过风波

paraphrase.intent: 想说「靠多条收入线才能活下来」
phrases: The shop survived because it walked on several legs.
No single revenue stream could carry it — so it had many.
paraphrase.chunks: walk on several legs · revenue stream
paraphrase.usage: walk on several legs 是口语里的俗语感；revenue stream 偏商业术语

paraphrase.intent: 想说「被法规逼得想关门」
phrases: The regulations pushed her to the point of just quitting.
She was almost driven out of business by red tape.
paraphrase.chunks: be driven to the point of · red tape
paraphrase.usage: red tape 指繁琐的法规/官僚程序，很地道

scenes.title_cn: 七、滤镜与真相：不要拿时代的名字套用 [23:24]
scenes.title_en: Filter vs. Reality: Don't Pin an Era's Name on Her
scenes.context: Netizens who visited the Witch House complained it was 'chaotic, indifferent, arrogant' — the romantic expectation fell flat. Panai offers another reading: no one is treated differently here. The hosts reflect on the gap between the era's name and today's reality. 语域：反思性评论 + 个人观点。
scenes.speak: As the hosts dug into the Witch House, their rosy filter only faded. Some netizens who visited complained it was 'chaotic, indifferent, arrogant' — the literary-space expectations crumbled one by one. The hosts get that completely — Peng herself admits the Witch House's 'grumpy face' is famous in the industry, and in an era of ever-more-polished service, it does pale next to all those refined, considerate stores. The key insight — Panai, an artist who grew out of the Witch House, offers another reading: 'The Witch House doesn't treat people differently — you're a guest, but you're still a person. The little witch who comes to work, she's a person too; she doesn't have to smile.' In this space, you're not extra great because you're a consumer, and no one becomes lesser because of the kind of work they do. Typical scenario: when you evaluate a space, separate 'service experience' from 'the value of the space' — do you expect to be served, or to be treated as a person? Quote from Panai: 'The Witch House doesn't treat people differently — you're a guest, but you're still a person. The little witch who comes to work is also a person; she doesn't have to wear a smile.' Quote from the show: 'In this space, you're not great just because you're a consumer, and people don't become lesser because of the nature of their work.' The host admits that putting the netizens' complaints and Panai's words side by side risks 'switching the subject' — but her view is: maybe it's better not to pin the name the era gave the Witch House onto her today, because there will always come a day when she falls short of the expectation. What the Witch House was first known and hoped for was never warmth or service, but the fact that she generously took in one musician after another who chose her — letting them be themselves, say their own piece, tell their own story — and welcomed them home again and again when they sailed back.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：主播在研究女巫店的过程中，对它的滤镜只减不增：有网友去了之后吐槽女巫店「混乱冷漠傲慢」，对文艺空间的期待一一落空。主播很能理解这种感受——彭郁晶也承认女巫店的臭脸在业界出了名，在服务业越来越卷的当下，确实与其他精致周到的店相形见绌
sentences.en: The more the hosts researched the Witch House, the more their romantic filter faded. Netizens who visited called it 'chaotic, indifferent, arrogant' — expectations of a literary space fell flat one by one. The hosts completely get that feeling: Peng herself admits the Witch House's grumpy face is famous in the industry, and in an era where service is getting more and more polished, it does look small next to those refined, considerate shops.
sentences.note: 表达提示rosy filter / romantic filter → 滤镜/美化；fall flat → 落空；grumpy face → 臭脸；pale next to → 与…相形见绌；polished service → 精致的服务

sentences.cn: 关键理解：从女巫店长起来的歌手巴奈给了另一种解读：「女巫店没有把人差别看待——你是客人，但你还是个人。小女巫来工作，她也是个人，她不一定要面带微笑。」这个空间里没有因为你是消费者就特别伟大，人也不会因为工作的性质变得比较低
sentences.en: The key insight — Panai, an artist who grew out of the Witch House, offers another reading: 'The Witch House doesn't treat people differently — you're a guest, but you're still a person. The little witch who comes to work, she's a person too; she doesn't have to smile.' In this space, you're not extra great because you're a consumer, and no one becomes lesser because of the kind of work they do.
sentences.note: 表达提示grow out of → 从…成长起来；another reading → 另一种解读；treat people differently → 差别看待；be lesser → 变低一等

sentences.cn: 典型场景：评估一个空间时，把「服务体验」与「空间价值」分开看待——你期待的是被招待，还是被当人？
sentences.en: Typical scenario: when you evaluate a space, separate 'service experience' from 'the value of the space' — do you expect to be served, or to be treated as a person?
sentences.note: 表达提示evaluate / assess → 评估；separate A from B → 把A与B分开；be treated as a person → 被当人看

sentences.cn: （引用）「女巫店没有把人差别看待，你是客人但你还是个人。小女巫来工作，她也是个人，她不一定要面带微笑。」——巴奈
sentences.en: Quote from Panai: 'The Witch House doesn't treat people differently — you're a guest, but you're still a person. The little witch who comes to work is also a person; she doesn't have to wear a smile.'
sentences.note: 表达提示wear a smile → 面带微笑（wear 表示刻意维持）；doesn't have to → 不一定要

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据：「这个空间里面没有因为你是消费者就特别伟大，人也不会因为工作的性质变得比较低。」
sentences.en: Quote from the show: 'In this space, you're not great just because you're a consumer, and people don't become lesser because of the nature of their work.'
sentences.note: 表达提示by the nature of one's work → 因工作性质；not great just because … → 不会因为…就特别伟大；the nature of → …的本质

sentences.cn: 核心机制：主播坦言把网友吐槽与巴奈的话放在一起有「偷换概念」的嫌疑，但她的观点是：也许不要去拿时代赋予女巫店的姓名去套在如今她的头上会比较好，因为永远会有错位、对不起预期的那一天。女巫店最初被知道和期待的，其实不是温暖与服务，而是她大方地接纳了一个又一个选择女巫店的音乐人，让他们可以做自己、说出自己的声音、讲出自己的故事，并在他们远航之后一次次迎接回航
sentences.en: The host admits that putting the netizens' complaints and Panai's words side by side risks 'switching the subject' — but her view is: maybe it's better not to pin the name the era gave the Witch House onto her today, because there will always come a day when she falls short of the expectation. What the Witch House was first known and hoped for was never warmth or service, but the fact that she generously took in one musician after another who chose her — letting them be themselves, say their own piece, tell their own story — and welcomed them home again and again when they sailed back.
sentences.note: 表达提示side by side → 并排对照；switch the subject → 偷换概念；pin A onto B → 把A安在B头上；fall short of expectations → 对不起预期；take in → 接纳；sail back → 回航

phrases: The fantasy didn't survive a single visit.
Reality slowly chipped away at their rosy image of the place.
paraphrase.chunks: didn't survive a visit · chip away at
paraphrase.usage: chip away at 有慢慢侵蚀的画面感；didn't survive 更犀利

paraphrase.intent: 想说「不要用时代的名字套现在」
phrases: Don't hold today's Witch House to the name an era gave her.
The label fits the era, not necessarily the shop.
paraphrase.chunks: hold A to B · the label fits … not necessarily …
paraphrase.usage: hold sb to sth 指用标准去要求某人；not necessarily 是口语常用来缓和的词

practice.cn: 用「not think twice」说：彭郁晶没多想就答应了阿峰。
practice.en: Peng didn't think twice before saying yes to A-Feng.

practice.cn: 用「less A than B」说：不插电与其说是立场，不如说是被邻居逼出的妥协。
practice.en: Unplugged was less a musical stance than a compromise forced by the neighbors.

practice.cn: 用「on the house」说：把内衣挂上椅子，饮料免费。
practice.en: Hang your bra on the chair and your drink is on the house.

practice.cn: 用「walk on several legs」说：女巫店靠多条收入线活了下来。
practice.en: The Witch House survived by walking on several legs.

pitfalls.wrong: The show lifted martial law in 1987.
pitfalls.why: lift 的主语是政府/地区，不是节目；The show/host 只能做引述主体（the host says…），不能替代政策主体。

pitfalls.wrong: A-Feng paid a Mercedes for the venue.
pitfalls.right: A-Feng lost a Mercedes to the venue's debts.
pitfalls.why: pay 语义是「付钱购买」；「赔进去/倒贴」用 lose … to / sink money into 更准确。

pitfalls.wrong: The unplugged rule is the shop's musical standpoint.
pitfalls.right: Unplugged wasn't a musical standpoint — it was a compromise the noise forced.
pitfalls.why: 把「被现状逼出来的妥协」说成主动立场（standpoint）丢掉了关键的被动性；用 not A but B 结构补出被动来源。

pitfalls.wrong: Female artists can only play on the stage on Witch Festival day.
pitfalls.right: Once a month, Witch Festival gives the stage to female artists only.
pitfalls.why: play on the stage 太直译；give the stage to sb 表达「让位」的机制感，once a month 才是准确的频次。

shifts.before: 以为女巫店是精心策划的商业产物
shifts.after: 它是被现实一步步「逼出来」的空间——器材、噪音、法规都成了它的设计者

shifts.before: 以为「不插电」是艺术坚持
shifts.after: 它本质是「怕吵到邻居」的妥协，但妥协反而把它逼上了亲密感与技巧的差异化赛道
多元收入是组织层面的冗余设计，让它三十年还活着，还给新人留了喘息空间
